item.title: #3586448: Disable agent subscriptions for Languages and gate Specific Entities on availability
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Major task
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3586448 · 1 contributor · 15 comments

Summary

In AI Context, agents can no longer subscribe to Languages. A language tag on an item no longer ranks it higher for an agent. Items are still dropped when the request language doesn't match, and they are still included in Relevant and Broad when it does. In Minimal mode, items tagged only with a language are no longer injected unless they use Always include. Existing language subscriptions stay in agent config but are ignored. Sites without Dynamic Entity Reference now list Specific Entities as Unavailable on the scope overview, where it used to be missing. Rebuild caches after updating. No update hook or config change is needed.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Config change: No config change; existing agent scope_subscriptions.language values are preserved but ignored.
  • New API: getParticipatingSubscriptions() added to the @internal AiContextScopeResolverInterface; ai_context_ai_context_scope_info_alter() is no longer implemented.

Technical details

Languages now overrides supportsSubscriptions() to FALSE and keeps supportsSituationalMatch() as TRUE, so its capability row is language => [FALSE, FALSE, TRUE]. The request language from AiContextLanguageService::detect() is always known, so matchesRequestContext() is never NULL. A subscription could only re-rank items and never broaden reach, the same reasoning as Roles. Form hiding, the "do not allow subscriptions" note, the scoring skip and save-time preservation of stored values follow from the capability.

Changing the capability alone leaked language-only items into Minimal. prefilterItemIdsByScope() is also used for Global index lookup, so non-subscription scopes can't be stripped inside it. The internal resolver (@internal AiContextScopeResolverInterface) gains getParticipatingSubscriptions(). It drops empty lists and scopes that are disabled, unavailable or supportsSubscriptions(): FALSE. The selector and budget calculator call it before prefilter and subscribed-ID resolution. This also fixes the same leak for stored Roles subscriptions.

Specific Entities was handled differently from Languages: ai_context_ai_context_scope_info_alter() removed its entity_item definition when dynamic_entity_reference was missing. That made its capability unreadable, so calculateScopeScore() carried a hardcoded skip list (global, entity_item, target_entity). Now AiContextScopeEntityItem::isAvailable() reports whether DER is installed, the alter hook implementation is removed, and the skip list is gone. Scoring and getParticipatingSubscriptions() decide purely by capability. A stored entity_item subscription on a non-DER site previously scored at the minimum weight and diluted other dimensions (90/91 instead of 90/90). Because the settings tab is now reachable while the scope is unavailable, validateSettingsForm() no longer queries the missing entity_items field, which otherwise threw a QueryException. The local task deriver is the one getScopePlugins() consumer that doesn't gate on availability, so the tab shows up.

Upgrade

Rebuild caches (drush cr) after deploying so plugin definitions and the agent form pick up the new capability and availability. Stored scope_subscriptions.language values on agents are kept but have no effect.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: August 23, 2026

Key contributors

  • kristen pol (Itty Bitty Byte)
  • tormi (Mearra (formerly known as Wunder))
  • pravesh_poonia (OpenSense Labs)

item.title: #3586388: Align scope scoring, language service, and contextual selection behavior
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Major task
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3586388 · 1 contributor · 28 comments

Summary

Scope ordering, subscription scoring and language handling in AI Context now follow one rule. A scope plugin's weight sets both its position in the UI and its influence on scoring, and higher values come first. Entity Bundle and Site Section scoped items are now excluded when no entity or request is available, instead of staying eligible. Content language is now detected the same way for selection, the language scope, and the list and load-by-id function calls. This includes AJAX calls that carry the language only in the Referer header.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: Scope plugin weight now means higher = displayed first and scored more strongly (previously lower = first). The AiContextScope attribute default weight changed from 0 to 1, and AiContextScopeBase::getWeight() falls back to 1.
  • New API: New ai_context.detected_language cache context, used by selection cache metadata.

Technical details

Built-in weights are now Global 100, Use Case 70, Entity Type (shown as Entity Bundle) 60, Site Section 50, Tag 40, Language 30 and Specific Entities (entity_item) 10. Scores use the weight directly through a max(1, weight) clamp in AiContextScopeResolver, replacing abs(weight) + 1. Scoring skips scopes where supportsSubscriptions() is FALSE. For plugin IDs with no plugin instance it also skips global, entity_item and target_entity. AiContextScopeManager sorts by weight descending with plugin ID as the tiebreaker. It no longer lists ai_context provider plugins before other modules, so custom plugins can fall between built-ins.

The new Drupal\ai_context\Service\AiContextLanguageService (ai_context.language_service, marked @internal) provides detect(), translateItem() and translateItems(). It replaces AiContextLanguageDetectorTrait, which is deleted, and the private translateItems() copies in AiContextSelector and LoadAiContextItemById. AiContextSelector, AiContextScopeLanguage, ListAiContextItems and LoadAiContextItemById all use it. The AiContextSelector constructor now takes the language service in place of LanguageManagerInterface. AiContextItemRevisionOverviewForm drops its unused languageManager argument. A new AiContextDetectedLanguageCacheContext returns detect() as its value and itself depends on languages:language_content and url.path. AiContextSelector now uses it in place of languages:language_content.

AiContextScopeEntityType gains matchesCurrentContext(): no item values gives NULL (neutral), no current value gives FALSE, otherwise a match test. AiContextScopeSiteSection returns FALSE instead of NULL when there is no current request. ListAiContextItems seeds the current entity from entity_type and entity_id through AiContextCurrentEntityResolver::setCurrentEntity() before filterByCurrentContext(), and clears it in a finally block.

Upgrade

Custom scope plugins that declared a weight for the old "lower is first" ordering need new values. For example, the built-in plugins changed like this:

// AiContextScopeGlobal
weight: 100,   // was -100
// AiContextScopeUseCase
weight: 70,    // was -10
// AiContextScopeLanguage
weight: 30,    // was 0

Pick a value between the built-in weights (for example 65, between Use Case and Entity Bundle) to place a custom scope. Code that calls ListAiContextItems for bundle-scoped content must pass entity_type and entity_id, because bundle-scoped items are now rejected when no entity can be resolved.

item.title: #3586207: Conditional Subcontext Provider Calls
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal task
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3586207 · 1 contributor · 40 comments

Summary

Conditional subcontext children used to cost one synchronous AI provider call per selected parent, which could dominate agent latency and provider usage. There are now two new settings on the Context item settings page (/admin/config/ai/context/settings/items). One turns AI decisions for conditional children on or off. The other caps how many parents get an AI decision per context resolution (default 3, range 1 to 20). The toggle defaults to on, so existing behavior is preserved apart from the new cap of 3. If AI decisions are off, all conditional children are included with no provider call. Parents over the cap keep their required children, but their conditional children are dropped. Identical decisions within one request are cached.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Database update: ai_context_update_10010() adds the two new settings to existing sites.
  • Config change: New ai_context.settings keys conditional_subcontext_enabled (default true) and conditional_max_parents (default 3, range 1 to 20); subcontext_enabled checkbox moved to the Context item settings form.

Technical details

AiContextSubcontextResolver::resolve() reads conditional_subcontext_enabled and conditional_max_parents (clamped to 1..20) and passes a by-reference $conditional_calls_made counter through resolveForParent() into resolveConditionalChildren(). The cap is checked before any prompt or provider work. Once reached, the parent's conditional children are dropped and an info message is logged. Which parents are dropped follows internal processing order, not relevance to the task. Calls are one per parent and are not batched.

A per-instance $decisionCache is keyed by md5(parent id | task | sorted candidate ids). It stores approved results, and it also stores empty results from a missing provider, a provider with no chat(), a bad response or an exception, so a broken provider is not re-hit within the request. Cap skips are deliberately not cached. A later resolve() call with budget left can still make the call.

The form layout changed too. The subcontext_enabled checkbox moved from AiContextSettingsForm to AiContextItemSettingsForm, which gains the two new fields with #states visibility. The provider field in AiContextSettingsForm gets a - None - option. Clearing the provider is now blocked only when conditional AI decisions are enabled and published conditional items exist. The provider description now says whether AI decisions are on. Config schema adds the two keys, with a Range constraint of 1 to 20 on conditional_max_parents.

Upgrade

ai_context_update_10010() sets conditional_subcontext_enabled: true and conditional_max_parents: 3 in ai_context.settings when they are unset. Run drush updb. Sites exporting config should export the two new keys.

item.title: #3586416: Clean stale scope values when options are deleted
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3586416 · 1 contributor · 15 comments

Summary

Context items and agent subscriptions no longer keep scope values for options that have been removed. Deleting a content type, taxonomy term, vocabulary, context tag, language or role now removes that value from items, subscriptions and the scope index. Removing an entity type from Entity Types settings, or a site section from settings, does the same. Uninstalling a module that provided those options also triggers a scrub. Deleting a bundle keeps the type-level type:_all value, but removing the whole type from settings removes it. Use Case values are never scrubbed. After upgrading, run drush updatedb: a one-time post-update cleans up leftovers that already exist. Because updates normally run before config import, on a lower environment with a copied production database this scrub can remove values for options the import is about to add.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Database update: Post-update ai_context_post_update_0006_scrub_stale_scope_values() strips already-stale scope values from items, agent subscriptions and the scope index.
  • New API: New optional AiContextScopeStoredValueInterface for scope plugins whose options can disappear; new AiContextScopeCleanupService methods scrubScope(), scrubStaleScopeValues(), scrubScopesAfterEntityDelete(), scrubScopesAfterBundleDelete(), scrubScopeAfterSettingsChange().

Technical details

The existing ai_context.scope_cleanup service (AiContextScopeCleanupService) still only strips values. The decision about what is stale moved into scope plugins through the new optional AiContextScopeStoredValueInterface: getStaleStoredValues(), shouldScrubAfterEntityDelete(), getStaleStoredValuesForEntityDelete(), shouldScrubAfterBundleDelete() and shouldScrubAfterSettingsChange(). The service now takes plugin.manager.ai_context_scope, collects stored values from the scope index (new AiContextScopeIndexService::getIndexedScopeValues()) and from raw ai_context.agents subscriptions, then asks the plugin which are stale. AiContextScopeInterface is unchanged.

Triggers are generic and do not special-case plugin IDs: ai_context_entity_delete(), the new ai_context_entity_bundle_delete(), and the new ai_context_modules_uninstalled(). The last skips config sync and skips uninstalling ai_context itself. AiContextScopeConfigSubscriber now reacts to any ai_context.scope_settings.{plugin_id} save and skips it while config.installer isSyncing(), because a mid-import scrub would compare stored values to a half-imported environment. Bundle-delete hooks still run during sync.

Plugin policy: Language, Roles, Tag and Entity Types treat a value as stale if it is missing from getAlteredValues(), via the new AiContextScopeBase::getStoredValuesMissingFromAlteredValues(). Site Section also keeps custom: patterns. Taxonomy Terms keeps a value if the term exists and is not in the ai_context_tags vocabulary, or an alter hook added it. Term, language and role deletes return the deleted ID for a cheap strip. A vocabulary delete returns NULL for a full scan. Entity Types scrubs after a bundle delete only when that entity type is enabled in settings, and after any settings save. Use Case, Global and Entity Item do not implement the interface.

Upgrade

Run the new post-update after deploying:

drush updatedb -y
drush cr

ai_context_post_update_0006_scrub_stale_scope_values() runs against the environment as it exists at that moment, before drush config:import in standard pipelines. On a lower environment with a copied production database it can remove values for options that the pending import would add.

Custom scope plugins that can lose options can implement AiContextScopeStoredValueInterface (in the Drupal\ai_context\Plugin\AiContextScope namespace) alongside AiContextScopeInterface. Plugins that do not implement it are left alone.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: August 17, 2026

Key contributors

  • kristen pol (Itty Bitty Byte)
  • pravesh_poonia (OpenSense Labs)

item.title: #3586471: Fix CCC scope index, stored-value cleanup, and request matching
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Major bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3586471 · 1 contributor · 48 comments

Summary

Several scope-data bugs in AI Context are fixed. Saving a draft of a published item no longer rewrites the live scope index, so a published Global item stays findable by prefilters while a draft is pending. Unchecking an entity type on the Entity Types settings page is now blocked, with an error naming the usage, while context items or consumer subscriptions still reference it. Language values are no longer deleted on single-language sites. Deleting the last bundle of a type keeps type:_all. Taxonomy matching now uses the revision or translation of the requested entity, and language detection honours a caller-supplied path such as /es/.... The Global checkbox stays visible on the item form when the Global scope is disabled, so existing global items can be cleared. Inheriting subcontexts score using the parent's values when a scope plugin is missing.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Config change: Service ai_context.language_service now receives @ai_context.request_info_resolver instead of @request_stack.
  • New API: AiContextScopeCleanupService gains public getStoredValuesWithPrefix() and countStoredValueUsage(); AiContextScopeEntityType implements validateSettingsForm().

Technical details

Index: ai_context_ai_context_item_update() in ai_context.module returns early when !$entity->isDefaultRevision(). The cascade to inheriting children now runs only if the original revision was a default revision and its scope differs. Publishing a draft therefore no longer compares against a draft whose scope was never written to the children.

Cleanup: AiContextScopeEntityType::validateSettingsForm() collects stored values for removed types via AiContextScopeCleanupService::getStoredValuesWithPrefix(). It counts usage with countStoredValueUsage(), which skips inheriting subcontexts, and sets a form error. getContentEntityTypeOptions() keeps a configured type listed even with no bundles. getValues() keeps the All option for a bundled type with no bundles, so the generic stale-value diff never reports type:_all missing after the last bundle delete. Live and settings-change scrubs skip disabled or unavailable plugins. Entity and bundle delete scrubs still run regardless. This is documented on AiContextScopeStoredValueInterface: a plugin returning NULL from getStaleStoredValuesForEntityDelete() gets a full getStaleStoredValues() scan even while the scope is disabled.

Matching: AiContextScopeResolver scoring falls back to $item->getScopeItem()->getScopeValues() instead of the child's own empty scope. AiContextLanguageService now takes AiContextRequestInfoResolver (service definition changed) and extracts the language prefix from the single path returned by getPath(). Taxonomy changes are in AiContextScopeTaxonomy and AiContextRequestInfoResolver. The summary describes the intended behaviour; I did not read that diff in full.

Upgrade

If you construct AiContextLanguageService yourself or override its service definition, the third argument changes from @request_stack to @ai_context.request_info_resolver:

arguments:
  - '@config.factory'
  - '@language_manager'
  - '@ai_context.request_info_resolver'

Contribution

  • Opened: September 1, 2026

item.title: #3588981: Export skill-harness results as every_eval_ever 0.2.2 envelopes (to_eee.py covers only the Inspect path)
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Minor task
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3588981 · 1 contributor · 2 comments

Summary

The skill evals in ai_best_practices can now produce valid Every Eval Ever (EEE) 0.2.2 records, with one result per arm (with the skill and without it). They no longer end up in a format only this project can read. The issue was filed because the old compare.py output and the per-case judge output were not valid EEE envelopes, although some of them carried a 0.2.2 label. A new publish_results.py command also packages a run into a scrubbed public results set and uploads it to Hugging Face. This matters to people who run or publish the project's skill evals. It does not affect Drupal sites.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: New evals/inspect/publish_results.py command with run, build and upload stages; to_eee.py now splits control logs into one result per arm.

Technical details

The issue proposed a converter over the existing comparison JSON. The landed commit takes the Inspect path instead, which the issue describes as already covered by evals/inspect/to_eee.py. to_eee.py, a thin wrapper over the upstream every-eval-ever[inspect] converter, now splits a control task log into one evaluation result per arm. The control task runs each case with the skill (metadata["arm"] is on) and without it (off). A single accuracy over both arms would describe neither. split_control_arms() replaces the converter's mixed accuracy with per-arm results. Each arm result has its own evaluation_result_id of the form <evaluation_id>/<arm>, and the arm and condition are recorded in source_data.additional_details. _arm_outcomes() collects the pass/fail outcome per sample for each arm, epochs included.

evals/inspect/publish_results.py has three stages. run runs every skill with and without its skill for N epochs on one model. build writes scrubbed Inspect logs, data/<split>.jsonl with one row per graded answer, eee/<skill>/<developer>/<model>/<uuid>.json records, and a card template. It refuses to finish if it finds a home path or a credential-looking string. upload repeats that check, refuses a card that still contains TODO(publish) lines, and does a dry run unless --yes is passed. A new dataset is created private. The command needs the EEE extra (evals/requirements-eee.txt). I did not find an exporter for the compare.py or run-judges.py output in the repo. I did not check whether the schema_version label in run-judges.py and validate-judges.py was changed.

item.title: #3588982: Add a canvas-migration eval instrument (agentic site-to-Canvas migration grader)
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3588982 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

The AI Best Practices project gains a canvas-migration eval instrument for grading whether an AI agent really rebuilt a website homepage as Drupal Canvas components and pages. It checks the served page, screenshots and measured geometry, not the agent's own report. A run produces two separate results: a quality score and a set of validity gates. A failed gate invalidates the run but does not lower the score. Cases blocked by a broken tool are marked unmeasured and left out of the score. Some checks are calibrated to one specific source page (pixel widths, section order, image and SEO fields). Against other sites they will report calibration mismatches, not real migration defects.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: New eval set under evals/canvas-migration/ with an abp-eval front door (list / grade / run / view / show / export) and a run.py run-group executor.

Technical details

This is based on the issue description only. No diff or comments were available, and the default branch I cloned does not yet contain evals/canvas-migration/, so I could not check the code.

According to the description, the instrument reuses the repo's existing scoring core. It adds about 24 check probes covering layout, link integrity, images, SEO, geometry, secrets and served-page checks. It also adds a rubric catalogue and a 2-case sample dataset, and consumers bring their own eval set. Grading runs in a docker "referee" sidecar (Python, Node, Chromium, geometry measurer) that talks to the test bed's containers without being given the docker socket, so the system under test cannot tamper with it. The referee ships build-from-source only. A native Inspect AI runner covers the same cases and exports results in Every Eval Ever 0.2.2 format. A vendored GPL-2.0-or-later geom-probe measurer is isolated in its own commit for licence auditability.

The rubrics validate against the vendored Eval Commons Layer 1 schema and use only the canonical check kinds (command / target_match / score_delta). Per the description, the evals/<skill-name>/ layout convention gains one documented exception, an eval set not tied to a single skill, noted in AGENTS.md.

item.title: #3589007: composer reinstall and composer install --no-dev delete ai_best_practices.yaml and block the plugin
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3589007 · 1 contributor · 6 comments

Summary

Running composer reinstall drupal/ai_best_practices or composer install --no-dev (when the package is a dev requirement) no longer wipes the project's ai_best_practices.yaml or the plugin's entries in composer.json. Before the fix, those commands removed the package's allow-plugins entry, so the next composer install failed with a "plugin blocked by your allow-plugins config" error, and any customizations in ai_best_practices.yaml were lost. Cleanup still runs on a real composer remove.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

Composer calls PluginInterface::uninstall() for the first half of a reinstall and for dev packages dropped by --no-dev, not only when the package is removed. AiBestPracticesPlugin::uninstall() now calls a new private packageStaysInstalled() and returns early, with a verbose-only message, if it reports true. The check relies on Composer writing the lock (or holding it in memory with lock: false) before running package operations, so the lock reflects the post-command project. It looks for the package name in the lock's packages and packages-dev sections. If there is no usable lock, or reading it throws, it falls back to the root package's require and require-dev. Transitive installs are covered because the lock lists them too. A new AiBestPracticesPluginUninstallTest covers the behavior.

Upgrade

If a project already hit this and the allow-plugins entry was removed, restore it with composer config allow-plugins.drupal/ai_best_practices true (the entry the issue says gets removed), or follow the workaround in #3588983 of deleting vendor/drupal/ai_best_practices and running composer install.

item.title: #3583075: Rename ContextDefinitionNormalizer now that it normalizes input and output definitions
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal task
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3583075 · 1 contributor · 5 comments

Summary

The Tool module's JSON Schema builder for input and output definitions is renamed from ContextDefinitionNormalizer to InputOutputDefinitionNormalizer. The old name described core's context system, which the definition families no longer build on. The old class name and service ID keep working for one release but trigger deprecation notices. Behavior is unchanged. Custom code that extends the class, uses its constants, or injects it by service ID should switch to the new names before rc1.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: The JSON Schema normalizer for input and output definitions is now Drupal\tool\Normalizer\InputOutputDefinitionNormalizer, with the same DECIMAL_PATTERN and DERIVED_ENUM_LIMIT constants.
  • Deprecation: Drupal\tool\Normalizer\ContextDefinitionNormalizer and the tool.normalizer.context_definition service are deprecated in tool:1.0.0-beta12 and removed from tool:1.0.0-rc1. Use InputOutputDefinitionNormalizer and tool.normalizer.input_output_definition.

Technical details

The full implementation moved into src/Normalizer/InputOutputDefinitionNormalizer.php. Its docblock now names the input and output definition families as the subject. Core ContextDefinitionInterface support is described as the ai module's override path. ContextDefinitionNormalizer stays as a thin shell that extends the new class. Its constructor calls @trigger_error() with E_USER_DEPRECATED, and its docblock carries @deprecated in tool:1.0.0-beta12 and is removed from tool:1.0.0-rc1.

In tool.services.yml the service is now tool.normalizer.input_output_definition, still tagged normalizer with priority 100. tool.normalizer.context_definition stays as a private alias with a deprecated message. Normalizers are private services, so the old ID resolves only where another service definition injects it by ID. A new kernel test, ContextDefinitionNormalizerDeprecationTest, covers the class and alias deprecations. Internal references were updated: LegacyTypedDataNormalizer uses InputOutputDefinitionNormalizer::DECIMAL_PATTERN, and comments in EntityHandleTransformer and EffectiveDataDefinition plus NormalizerFormatRestrictionTest were changed to match. The issue body says tool_belt, canvas_tools and mcp_server_tool_bridge do not refer to the old class or service ID.

Upgrade

Replace the class and service references:

// Before
use Drupal\tool\Normalizer\ContextDefinitionNormalizer;
// After
use Drupal\tool\Normalizer\InputOutputDefinitionNormalizer;

# Before
arguments: ['@tool.normalizer.context_definition']
# After
arguments: ['@tool.normalizer.input_output_definition']

item.title: #3589004: Eval runner: add a Kiro CLI provider
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3589004 · 1 contributor · 4 comments

Summary

Behavioral evals can now run against Kiro CLI as well as claude, codex, gemini and mistral. Run python3 evals/run-evals.py --behavioral --skill <skill> --provider kiro to see whether a skill changes Kiro's answers. Kiro runs answer-only with no tools trusted. It needs kiro-cli 2.31 or later, and you log in with kiro-cli login or set KIRO_API_KEY. Kiro reports credits rather than tokens, so runs show no token or cost figures.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: New kiro provider for the behavioral eval runner (--provider kiro, Inspect model string abp_cli/kiro), default model claude-sonnet-5.

Technical details

The provider is run_kiro() in evals/providers.py, registered in PROVIDERS, PROVIDER_DEFAULTS and ISOLATION_MODES. It calls kiro-cli chat --agent-engine v3 --no-interactive --trust-tools= --output-format stream-json --model <model> from a fresh temporary directory. The merged code differs from the issue text: the prompt goes on stdin rather than after --, which also avoids Kiro parsing the skill's --- frontmatter as an option. The output is stream-json, not plain text. The default model is claude-sonnet-5, not auto, because auto picks a model per task and runs would not compare.

Older kiro-cli releases leave their agent server running with the inherited stdout, so stdout and stderr go to temp files, the process is started in its own session, and the whole process group is killed after wait(). The answer comes from the runFinished event's finalText. If that is truncated or missing, the agent_message_chunk updates are joined instead.

Each call gets a throwaway KIRO_HOME, so the operator's ~/.kiro steering, skills and agents do not load. _kiro_context() reads the steering from the session log under KIRO_HOME and the skills and agents from the stream's command list. It raises ContextLeakError for anything that is not bundled with Kiro, or when no session log exists. Per the docs, kiro-cli 2.16 still read ~/.kiro with KIRO_HOME set, so it is unsupported. test_scoring.py tests this against a fake kiro-cli. CONTRIBUTING.md, evals/inspect/README.md and evals/inspect/to_eee.py were updated for the new provider.

Install kiro-cli 2.31 or later, then run:

item.title: #3586791: Add Refusal Answer type to support OpenAI Decision API
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3586791 · 1 contributor · 6 comments

Summary

The AI module's Decision operation can now represent a model declining to answer an individual question. Previously a refusal, which OpenAI's Decision API can return, was treated as broken output and failed the whole response. Models that declare the new decision_refusals capability may now refuse single questions while the other answers stay usable. Refusals from models that don't declare it still count as broken output.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: AnswerValidation::forQuestion() gains an optional third parameter $allow_refusal (default FALSE); AnswerFactory::fromArray() accepts a refusal type.
  • New API: New RefusalAnswer value, AiModelCapability::DecisionRefusals, AiDecisionRefusedException, and DecisionResponse::isRefused() / getRefusals().

Technical details

A new final class Drupal\ai\OperationType\Decision\Value\RefusalAnswer implements AnswerInterface. Its type is 'refusal' (RefusalAnswer::TYPE), getRaw() keeps the provider's wire data, and toArray() returns only ['type' => 'refusal']. AnswerFactory::fromArray() gains a refusal case.

AnswerValidation::forQuestion() takes a third parameter bool $allow_refusal = FALSE. A RefusalAnswer is accepted for any question type when it is TRUE, and otherwise throws \InvalidArgumentException. DecisionValidationEventSubscriber::postGenerate() only resolves the model's capabilities when the answer is a refusal. It checks the provider's getDecisionCapabilities() for AiModelCapability::DecisionRefusals. If the provider or model can't be resolved, it counts as not declared, and the InvalidArgumentException becomes AiBrokenOutputException.

On DecisionResponse, isRefused($id) and getRefusals() (question ids) were added. getNoul(), getChoice() and getScore() now throw the new AiDecisionRefusedException (an \UnexpectedValueException implementing AiExceptionInterface) when the question was refused, instead of the type-mismatch error. The capability's enum value is decision_refusals, in the decision operation type group.

Upgrade

Provider authors whose Decision API can decline a question should declare the capability and return a refusal answer:

AiModelCapability::DecisionRefusals
// wire answer: ['type' => 'refusal', ...]; AnswerFactory::fromArray() turns it into RefusalAnswer

Callers of DecisionResponse should check isRefused($id) or getRefusals() before calling getNoul(), getChoice() or getScore(), or catch AiDecisionRefusedException.

item.title: #3586784: Let Decision models declare a minimum number of choice options
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3586784 · 1 contributor · 18 comments

Summary

Decision providers can now declare a minimum number of options for choice questions. Some backends need at least two options and previously could only fail after a round trip to the server, because the shared contract suite assumed a single option was valid. With a declared minimum, a choice question with too few options is rejected with AiBadRequestException before anything is sent. The provider's capability details now show the minimum next to the maximum. Existing declarations keep working unchanged.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: DecisionCapabilities gains a trailing nullable constructor argument and public property minChoiceOptions (NULL means unknown, a single option is accepted).

Technical details

DecisionCapabilities takes ?int $minChoiceOptions = NULL as the last constructor argument. The constructor throws \InvalidArgumentException if a minimum is set without DecisionChoice support, is below 1, or exceeds maxChoiceOptions. DecisionRequestValidator::validate() calls a new private checkMinimum() for choice questions, throwing AiBadRequestException ("supplied N choice options; the minimum is M") before the existing maximum check. An unknown (NULL) minimum is left to the provider.

DecisionCapabilityDetails::limits() now prints "Choice options: minimum X, maximum Y" (or "maximum Y", or "not supported" when choice is not declared). It also reports "not supported" for score levels when score is not declared. The markup string changed from "Maximum choice options: ..." to "Choice options: ...".

On the test side, DecisionContractCases builds choice questions with max(1, minChoiceOptions) options. boundaries() adds an accepted choices/<min> case and a rejected choices/<min - 1> case when the minimum is above 1. DecisionProviderContractTestBase::testDecisionDeclarationsAndDiscovery() now compares minChoiceOptions too. docs/developers/decision_provider_contract.md and call_decision.md document the limit.

Upgrade

Providers whose models need more than one choice option can declare it in their capabilities, for example:

new DecisionCapabilities([Capability::DecisionChoice], maxChoiceOptions: 26, minChoiceOptions: 2)

Providers that currently map a server 4xx for too few options can drop that workaround.

item.title: #3585947: Multi-round elicitation fails on protocol 2026-07-28 without a request state signing key
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Major bug report
  • Version: 2.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3585947 · 1 contributor · 10 comments

Summary

On MCP protocol 2026-07-28, a tool that asks the client more than one question in a single tools/call used to fail on the second question with a "could not carry its own state" internal error. The module now signs the state that carries earlier answers between rounds, so multi-round elicitation works. No new setting is needed. Tools that elicit only once were not affected.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

Under 2026-07-28 there are no server-to-client requests. ClientGateway::elicit() ends the call with an InputRequiredResult, the client resends the whole call, and the tool reruns from the top. Earlier answers travel in a signed requestState. The SDK needs an HMAC key from Builder::setRequestState(), which McpServerFactory never called.

McpServerFactory now takes @private_key as a new last constructor argument (mcp_server.services.yml is updated). It calls $builder->setRequestState() with Crypt::hmacBase64('mcp_server.request_state', $this->privateKey->get() . Settings::getHashSalt()). This is the same derivation style as core's CsrfTokenGenerator. The key comes from secrets shared across web heads, so a retry can land on any of them. The call is wrapped in method_exists($builder, 'setRequestState'), because mcp/sdk 0.7 predates this protocol version and has no such method.

Rotating the private key or hash salt only invalidates multi-round calls in progress. The issue cites the SDK's 10-minute TTL for this state. The commit adds a fixture tool, ElicitingTwiceTool, and a 2026-07-28 tools/call test in McpServerFunctionalTest that answers both rounds.
